detailed_findings.finding: The inequality d >= r - s is invoked as 'triangle inequality'; more precisely it is the reverse triangle inequality. This is only a wording issue and does not affect correctness.

The construction of A,B depends on a chosen orthonormal basis with first axis along OX; this is mathematically standard in R^2 and sufficient for the natural-language proof, though Lean formalization may prefer a coordinate-free reformulation.

reason: The proof gives a correct explicit construction for any chosen X on Circle(G,s): since dist(O,X) > r/2, the parameters m = r^2/(2d) and h = sqrt(r^2 - m^2) are well-defined with h > 0, yielding distinct A,B on Circle(O,r) such that dist(X,O)=dist(X,A)=dist(X,B), and O,A,B are noncollinear, so X is the circumcenter. The recursive step is also sound: only finitely many points of Circle(G,s) must be excluded to avoid reusing any previously chosen A_i or B_i, because for each prior Y the bad X lie in Circle(G,s) ∩ l_Y where l_Y is the perpendicular bisector of OY, hence at most two points. This preserves pairwise distinctness of the X_i and of all ten A_i,B_i. The argument matches the stated lemma and intended role.
